newsitem.title: UKRAINE: NATO wants special Ukraine deal, says Portillo.
newsitem.headline: NATO wants special Ukraine deal, says Portillo.

text.p: British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said on Sunday that NATO countries were keen to make a special deal with Ukraine and he hoped it would be ready for a European security summit in July.
"Britain in common with other NATO partners is very enthusiastic about making a new arrangement between NATO and Ukraine," he said at the start of a two-day visit to the former Soviet republic.
"I believe that these discussions are proceeding well and I very much hope that these can be brought to a conclusion by the time of the NATO Madrid summit."

Portillo was speaking to reporters after meeting Defence Minister Olexander Kuzmuk and security chief Volodymyr Horbulin to discuss Kiev's role in the alliance's plans to admit new members from eastern Europe.
Ukraine has no immediate hope of joining the 16-member North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, but unlike Russia it does not oppose NATO expansion.
"It may be our strategic desire, our strategic plan, but today Ukraine is not ready to join NATO. This must be understood," Horbulin told reporters later in his office.
The Madrid summit is expected to invite one or more countries to join NATO by 1999, while signing a charter with Russia designed to calm its fears about NATO expansion.

At the same time, Portillo said, a deal with Ukraine would give the two sides a chance to discuss shared problems. "We would examine together threats to world peace and we would discuss where action together was appropriate," he said.
Horbulin said Portillo had shown "even more understanding than I expected" and described their meeting as constructive.

Kiev wants security guarantees of its own. In particular it wants a nuclear-free zone in eastern Europe and has welcomed NATO promises not to put nuclear weapons on the territory of prospective new members such as Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic.
Ukraine once held more than 1,800 nuclear warheads but transferred the last of its share of the former Soviet nuclear arsenal to Russia for dismantling last year.

It participates in NATO's Partnership for Peace friendship programme and took part in exercises with British and Polish troops last year which Portillo said were "a clear sign of the strong and growing relationship between us."
Portillo is due to meet President Leonid Kuchma on Monday after the Ukrainian leader returns from the annual World Economic Reform in Switzerland.
